findings: The pinned 2026.4.1 runtime supports4096-pixel batches for all four captured compositor variants. Other runtime versions retain512.
Precision markers are checked after IR normalization through the public attribute visitor. The migrated value must prohibit conversion to f16; the check is not removed.

Integer-index bounds combine exact0/1 integer masks on the NPU instead of the miscompiled LogicalAnd graph. Lower/upper bounds, invalid-index rejection and zero-row fallback remain enabled for every shader. The earlier shader-specific coefficient bypass is removed; original scalar tolerances are unchanged.

All20 new-runtime rendering checks, the repeated eight-model cache hit/pixel check, both complete captured desktop draw oracles, the driver draw/clear test, four legacy NPU compatibility tests and all17 prewarm packet comparisons pass. These qualify the renderer for an installed experiment, not full desktop offload or a Tahoma speedup.
Cache entries are isolated with SHA-256 of canonical graph structure, constants and runtime build. All eight solid rectangle models pass exact pixel checks on both first compilation and cache reuse.

The guest UMD uses the legacy runtime closure; the host rendering worker uses2026.4.1. Both builds have identical source hashes and retain the same IPC contract. There is no CPU or GPU rendering fallback.

Intel emits internal function-outliner-vertical-fusion diagnostics in some passing shader suites. Those suites exit successfully, report NPU execution, and pass unchanged scalar oracles. Their complete logs are retained; diagnostics are not suppressed.
